questions.prompt: What is the difference between an attribute directive and a structural directive?

options.text: Attribute directives have templates; structural directives do not
An attribute directive changes its host element; a structural directive adds or removes views from a template
Structural directives can only be used on <div> elements
There is no difference; the names are interchangeable

questions.explanation: Attribute directives change the look or behavior of their host element. Structural directives (used with *) create and remove views from an <ng-template>.

questions.prompt: Which selector makes a directive apply to any element with an appHighlight attribute?
questions.explanation: Square brackets make it an attribute selector. 'appHighlight' without brackets would match an <appHighlight> element.

questions.prompt: Which @Directive property declares bindings and event listeners on the host element, e.g. { "(mouseenter)": "active.set(true)" }?
questions.explanation: The host property is the recommended replacement for the @HostBinding and @HostListener decorators.

questions.prompt: Match each API to its role in a structural directive.

pairs.right: The template the directive sits on

questions.explanation: A structural directive renders its TemplateRef into its ViewContainerRef, and clears it when the content should disappear.

questions.prompt: A component lists { directive: ClickOutside } in hostDirectives. Can its users write (appClickOutside)="close()"?

options.text: Yes, all host directive inputs and outputs are public
No, unless the output is listed in the entry's outputs array (optionally with an alias)
Only if the component also imports ClickOutside
No, host directives cannot have outputs

questions.explanation: A host directive's inputs and outputs are private unless you expose them, e.g. outputs: ['appClickOutside: dismissed'].

questions.prompt: Why should a structural directive avoid calling clear() and createEmbeddedView() on every change?

options.text: It is not allowed inside effect()
Rebuilding destroys and recreates the content, losing focus and component state
createEmbeddedView() can only be called once per app

questions.explanation: Track whether the view exists, create it once when needed, and clear it once when it should go away.
